To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the spectral resolution in a plane grated monochromator can be improved by a factor of about 10 by operating the monochromator in a divergent, instead of a collimated, incident beam, when an astigmatic mirror pair is used for correcting the aberrations in the diffraction.

the spectral resolution of an off-plane diffraction monochromator is limited by the source size and can be improved by using an uncollimated divergent incident beam, which can be achieved by using an astigmatic focusing mirror system.
the use of an uncollimated divergent incident beam can be used to obtain high spectral resolution in a plane grated monochromator when the incident beam is directed parallel to the groove direction.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the design and development of a monochromators for high spectral resolution in the extreme ultraviolet/ soft X-ray range based on the concept of off-plane diffraction with astigmatic focusing in an uncollinated incident beam.

the development of a high-resolution soft X-ray monochromatic for the study of synchrotron-radiation based experiments, which can be operated in a divergent beam and which provides high spectral resolution in a wide energy range.
the development of a new type of monochromator, which can provide high spectral resolution and high throughput simultaneously, and which can be used in the extreme ultraviolet/ soft X-ray region.

the spectral resolution is limited by the source size, not by aberrations in the optical system.

the use of a plane grating with a constant groove density in the off-plane configuration with a crossed mirror pair can be used to obtain source size limited spectral resolving power of the order of ΔE/E = 10000 in an uncolliminated incident beam, which is the same as that obtained in the conventional on-plane configuration with a collimated incident radiation.
the spectral resolution in a monochromatic beam is not degraded by the use of a divergent incident synchrotron beam, when the aberrations are corrected by astigmatic focusing.

the concept of off-plane diffraction with an uncollimated, divergent incident beam can be applied in a plane-grating monochromator with a sawtoogh profile and a constant groove density.

the spectral resolution in a plane grated monochromator operating with an uncollimated divergent beam is not necessarily worse than that in a collimated beam.
